chunks: Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
He was asked about hoarding, so he said:

Hoarding is only when you buy food while there is no other food in the town besides it, then you hoard it. But if there is other food or merchandise in the town besides it, then there is no harm in seeking profit through your goods.

key_terms.الْحُكْرَةُ: hoarding; withholding essential goods from the market during scarcity
key_terms.الْفَضْلَ: surplus or added profit sought in trade
key_terms.الْمِصْرِ: the town or locality in which availability is being considered
key_terms.بِسِلْعَتِكَ: through your merchandise; referring to one's tradable goods
key_terms.طَعَامًا: food; the commodity specifically mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.مَتَاعٌ: goods or merchandise other than food

ai.seo_question: When does hoarding food become prohibited in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith defines unlawful hoarding as withholding food when it is uniquely scarce in the town and people have no alternative source. If other food or goods are available, then seeking additional profit through one's merchandise is not considered problematic in this context.
